title: DALLE-2 is Seeing Double: Flaws in Word-to-Concept Mapping in Text2Image Models
role: The behavioural origin of 'concept leakage': hand-built challenge and control prompts on DALLE-2, including two-animal pairs where one animal's part appears on the other; no fix and no location inside the model.
enters: not located; text encoder or generative model left open
enters_evidence: Argument only: the paper says future work must trace whether the flaw stems from text encoding, the generative model, or both, cites the hypothesis that CLIP embeddings do not bind attributes, and reads the second-order prompts as the model mapping entities to concepts before rendering.
changes: Nothing; diagnosis only, post-hoc mitigation left to future work.
training: Nothing trained; images from the closed DALLE-2 product; no boxes, masks, parser or LLM; stimuli hand-written.
model: DALLE-2 (DALLE-mini and Stable Diffusion, version not printed, in unquantified preliminary runs)
similar_subjects: Two-animal prompts on DALLE-2, images showing one animal's property on the other out of 12: armadillo and elephant 12 vs rhino and elephant 0; fish and elephant 12 vs 0; leopard and a piece of cloth 11 vs leopard and a black towel 5; over 10 entity-to-property pairs 92.5% of images vs 6.6% for controls (higher is more leakage).
which_pairs: Argued: the receiving entity is underspecified and the leaked property suits it (gold onto fish, stripes onto street as a crosswalk); naming a specific kind removes it; rhino and elephant, a look-alike pair, leak in 0 of 12 images.
headline: On DALLE-2 an entity's property appeared on the other entity in 92.5% of images for 10 challenge prompts vs 6.6% for minimally changed controls (12 images per prompt, higher is more leakage); homonyms drew both senses in 80.3% of images.
suggests: Leakage in these rows rides on one subject having a distinctive transferable part, not on overall look-alikeness (rhino and elephant 0 of 12), so a 'transferable part' predictor and a modifier-added prompt control are worth adding beside the three similarity predictors (inferred).
